editorial.thesis: A workshop-and-food-and-drink city of about 5.2 million. Its retail is heavy on desserts, sweets & ice cream and cafés, tea & coffee, and thin on apparel, footwear & jewellery and grocery & daily needs — and 4% of residents live in zones with under 60% of the city's average retail depth.
takeaways: Branded retail is ahead of Delhi. 23.15 chain outlets per lakh residents against 18.83 in Delhi; 44 of the 51 national brands we track are present, led by Café Coffee Day 163, Domino's 106, Subway 80.

The mapped economy leans to desserts & sweets. Shares of all mapped places: desserts & sweets 1.1% (Delhi 0.7%); services & crafts 8.0% (Delhi 6.3%); malls & department stores 0.4% (Delhi 0.8%); automotive 2.2% (Delhi 3.0%). Raw counts would mislead because Delhi is mapped more completely (87,703 places against 67,726), so we compare mix, not counts.

Supply and demand are misaligned. 1 zones hold 4% of residents with under 60% of the city's average retail depth. Chembur Colony · Ramakrishna Chemburkar Marg alone has about 210,000 residents and 84 mapped food & drink places.

Retail is less concentrated than in Delhi. 38% of commercial places sit in the busiest tenth of the city (Delhi 47%). The largest cores are New Link Road · Veera Desai Road (3,244 places) and Hill Road · Linking Road (2,180).

The widest brand gaps against Delhi. Apollo Pharmacy 41 outlets vs 108; Haldiram's 5 outlets vs 44; Domino's 106 outlets vs 140. These are leads to check against live listings, not verdicts: a brand may trade under another name or have opened since the map was updated.

numbers.title: The city in eight numbers
numbers.deck: A 10 km circle around the centre, processed with the same rules as Delhi, so every comparison is like for like. Where raw counts would mislead — because a bigger city is mapped more completely — we compare shares and mix instead.

map.title: Where people live, where shops are
map.deck: Switch layers. The amber “gap” layer is the one to study: it marks places with many residents but little retail around them. Hover any hexagon (about 0.1 km²) for its numbers; click a zone on the right to isolate it.

captions.residents: Where people live. Saki Vihar Road · Andheri Kurla Road and Chembur Colony · Ramakrishna Chemburkar Marg are the largest zones by residents (216,000 and 210,000). Modelled residents per square kilometre.
captions.supply: Where the shops are. The busiest tenth of cells hold 38% of all commercial places, and New Link Road · Veera Desai Road alone lists 3,244.
captions.chains: Where the brands are. New Link Road · Veera Desai Road holds 67 of the 1206 tracked chain outlets, and Hill Road · Linking Road adds 54.
captions.education: Where the campuses are. New Link Road · Veera Desai Road and Sv Road · Veera Desai Road lead on education places (223 and 161, with 101 and 81 coaching centres) — a daytime youth market that residents alone do not show.
captions.gap: The gap. Amber: many residents nearby, little retail. Blue: far more retail than local residents explain — the commercial cores that draw people in. The deepest amber sits in Chembur Colony · Ramakrishna Chemburkar Marg. The blue cores include New Link Road · Veera Desai Road.

zones.title: Zone by zone, by PIN code
zones.deck: Each zone is a postal-code area. Residents are modelled counts; places are mapped businesses and services. “Retail depth” is places per 10,000 residents — the tick marks the city average. Click a row to see it on the map.

mix.title: What the retail layer is made of
mix.deck: Raw counts per resident would favour whichever city is mapped more completely (87,703 places in Delhi against 67,726 here). So this compares each category's share of all mapped places. 100 means the same share as Delhi; below 100 is thinner, above is stronger.
mix.note: Against Delhi, Mumbai's mapped places over-index on desserts & sweets (1.1% vs 0.7%), services & crafts (8.0% vs 6.3%), food & beverage (10.1% vs 8.0%) and under-index on malls & department stores (0.4% vs 0.8%), automotive (2.2% vs 3.0%), shops & retail (13.6% vs 17.2%).

chains.title: Who is mapped here, and who is not
chains.deck: 1206 outlets of 44 tracked national brands within 10 km — 23.15 per lakh residents against Delhi's 18.83 (1289 outlets of 45 brands). Filled names have at least one mapped outlet (count shown); dashed names have none.
chains.note: Read dashed names as leads, not verdicts. “No mapped outlet” can mean a brand trades under a different listed name, or has opened since the map was updated. The widest gaps against Delhi are Apollo Pharmacy (41 vs 108); Haldiram's (5 vs 44); Domino's (106 vs 140). Premium reports check every lead against live listings.

formats.title: Which formats have room
formats.deck: 9 formats, thinnest first. The index is the format's share of all mapped places relative to Delhi's, so low means thin by Delhi's standard. “Where to look” ranks zones with at least 40,000 residents by residents per mapped outlet — a first-pass screen for where one more outlet would face the least local competition.

people.title: Who the customers are
people.deck: Age mix inside the 10 km circle, from Meta's age rasters (modelled, not a census).
people.note: Mumbai's age mix against Delhi: children (0–14) 19.9% vs 23.1%, 15–24 19.7% vs 20.4%, working age 52.1% vs 49.7%, 60+ 8.4% vs 6.8%. Under-25s are 40% of residents.

restaurants.read: Restaurants & fast food are 7.0% of mapped places against 5.7% in Delhi — above its share. Mapped chain outlets: Domino's 106 (Delhi 140), Subway 80 (Delhi 55), McDonald's 71 (Delhi 75), Pizza Hut 49 (Delhi 68).
restaurants.watch: Independent eateries are numerous and unevenly mapped. Treat the index as a screen and confirm competitor density street by street.

cafes.read: Cafés, tea & coffee are 2.7% of mapped places against 2.1% in Delhi — above its share. Mapped chain outlets: Café Coffee Day 163 (Delhi 145), Starbucks 59 (Delhi 33), Chaayos 24 (Delhi 18), Blue Tokai 24 (Delhi 26).
cafes.watch: Chai stalls and independent cafés are under-mapped. A café concept here competes on price and habit as much as on novelty.

desserts.read: Desserts, sweets & ice cream are 1.1% of mapped places against 0.7% in Delhi — above its share. Mapped chain outlets: Baskin Robbins 55 (Delhi 29), Theobroma 21 (Delhi 11), Naturals 17 (Delhi 7), Havmor 11 (Delhi 6). No mapped outlet in either city: Cream Stone.
desserts.watch: Traditional sweet shops are the real benchmark and sit outside most chain lists.

grocery.read: Grocery & daily needs are 1.9% of mapped places against 2.2% in Delhi — below its share. Mapped chain outlets: DMart 25 (Delhi 7), Reliance Smart / Fresh 18 (Delhi 21), Big Bazaar 8 (Delhi 8), Spencer's 7 (Delhi 9).
grocery.watch: Neighbourhood kirana stores are the real incumbents and the least completely mapped outlets, so any gap is overstated. Test a site against local store density before acting.

pharmacy.read: Pharmacy & health retail are 1.3% of mapped places against 1.2% in Delhi, so the mix is level. Mapped chain outlets: Apollo Pharmacy 41 (Delhi 108), Wellness Forever 18 (Delhi 0), MedPlus 1 (Delhi 0). No mapped outlet in either city: Frank Ross.
pharmacy.watch: Independent chemists are dense and lightly mapped. Hospital and clinic clusters are the natural anchors.

apparel.read: Apparel, footwear & jewellery are 4.8% of mapped places against 7.0% in Delhi — below its share. Mapped chain outlets: Bata 52 (Delhi 66), Raymond 35 (Delhi 55), Titan 31 (Delhi 21), Tanishq 30 (Delhi 20).
apparel.watch: Established multi-brand traders and local bazaars sit behind these numbers; new entrants compete with them as well as with chains.

banking.read: Banks & ATMs are 7.8% of mapped places against 7.9% in Delhi, so the mix is level.
banking.watch: This category includes insurance and agency offices, so it overstates branch banking. Use it as a signal of commercial activity, not a branch count.

coaching.read: Coaching & training are 2.7% of mapped places against 2.7% in Delhi, so the mix is level.
coaching.watch: Coaching demand follows the exam calendar. Formats that depend on it should be tested across the academic year.

fitness.read: Fitness & wellness are 4.4% of mapped places against 3.9% in Delhi — above its share.
fitness.watch: Gym listings change often and are inconsistently categorised; verify before drawing conclusions.
